Welcome to %1$s! This replaces Android\'s screen rotation, so don\'t use the normal Android screen rotation settings.

There are two modes: %1$s and Locked. To see which one you\'re using, look at the notification in the notification drawer. In Locked mode, the notification shows the locked screen orientation, such as \"%2$s\".
To change mode, touch the notification. You can also make a home screen shortcut to do this.
In Locked mode, you can\'t change the screen orientation.
%1$s mode is the same as Android\'s screen rotation, but the screen faces you instead of the sky. For example, if %2$s thinks you\'re sideways, the screen will face sideways.
Your orientation (whether you\'re lying down or upright) is also tracked and shown in the notification.

To change your orientation, use Locked mode. In this mode, rotating the device will change whether %1$s thinks you\'re lying down or upright. It thinks you\'re facing the same direction as the screen. For example, if the screen is facing sideways, %1$s will think you\'re sideways.
%1$s might not work with apps that control the screen orientation. When this happens, the notification will show \"%2$s\".
To uninstall, use the \"%1$s\" menu item on %2$s\'s main screen so the screen orientation won\'t be stuck.
If the screen faces the wrong way:\n1. Turn %1$s mode off.\n2. Rotate the device until the screen is facing the right way.
